title: Test a prototype with users
summary: Watching real users try a prototype shows you what works before anything is built. Small, repeated rounds of testing are cheaper and more useful than one big study.

beginner: Agree what you want to learn from this round, for example 'Can people find out whether they are eligible?'. Keep it to two or three questions.
Ask your designer for a prototype that is just real enough to test those questions. It can be paper, clickable screens or a coded prototype.
Write 3 to 5 realistic tasks based on what users actually need to do. Do not give away the answer in the wording.
Recruit about 5 people from your main user group. If you have very different groups, use 3 or 4 from each.
In each session, ask people to think aloud while they try the tasks. Watch and listen. Do not help unless they are completely stuck.
Afterwards, list the problems you saw and how serious each one is. Agree changes with the team, update the prototype and test again.
intermediate: Set two or three learning goals and build a prototype only as real as those goals need.
Run moderated sessions with about 5 users per group, using realistic tasks.
Rate the problems found by severity and agree design changes with the team.
Plan the next round, so you test that the fixes worked.
experienced: Learning goals set; prototype fidelity matches them.
About 5 users per distinct group; tasks are realistic and neutral.
Issues rated, changes agreed, next round booked.
Engineering has confirmed the preferred design is feasible.

canDelegateTo.task: Build the prototype and update it between rounds
Recruit participants, write the tasks and moderate sessions
Write the words in the prototype and check they make sense to users
Check the design is feasible and flag anything costly to build

toolExamples.figma: Link frames into a clickable prototype and share a view-only link for remote sessions. Keep a page for each test round, so you can compare versions.
toolExamples.miro: Run a quick team debrief straight after each session: one sticky note per issue, then group by screen.
toolExamples.confluence: Keep a page per round with the goals, tasks, issues found and decisions made.
toolExamples.claude: Paste your draft tasks and ask whether any of them give away the answer or use your internal jargon.

definitionOfDone: At least one round tested with real users from the target group
Issues recorded and rated by severity
Preferred design judged feasible by engineering
pitfalls: Testing with colleagues instead of real users
Helping participants through the task, which hides the problems
Running one large study instead of several small rounds
